# twclock

**World clock for the operating position, with a CW station-ID timer**

- **Version recorded:** 3.5
- **Categories:** `cw`, `station`, `timing`
- **Upstream:** <https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/twclock>

## What it does

Shows UTC alongside several time zones you choose, and runs a countdown timer that sounds your callsign in Morse on the sound card when it expires -- speed and tone are adjustable. The Morse is generated by code shared with unixcw and qrq rather than by a recording.

## Why you would want it

Two things every operating position needs and neither is worth a browser tab. UTC because logs and schedules are in it and local time is a source of error; the ID timer because most licences require periodic identification and the interval is exactly the sort of thing that slips while you are concentrating on a contact.

## Before it will work

An X11 session with Motif, which Debian provides, and a working sound output for the ID. Your callsign has to be set in the program before the ID means anything.

## How it installs

- apt: `twclock`

## Known problems

It is a Motif application and looks it -- the widget set predates GTK, so it will not match any modern desktop theme and does not scale on HiDPI. The identification interval that satisfies your licence is a legal question this program does not know the answer to: it counts down from whatever you set, and setting it correctly is yours.
**Upstream is gone.** Debian declares the Homepage as wa0eir.bcts.info/twclock.html; that hostname does not resolve at all, and neither does the wa0eir.home.mchsi.com address in the package's copyright file (both checked 2026-08-28). The software works and is packaged; there is nowhere to report a bug except the distribution, and no new version is coming. Recorded rather than left for the next person to find from a browser error.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
- Whatever the distribution ships. Upstream is unreachable — see documentation.known_problems — so there is no upstream release to track and apt is the only source of a change.

## Where to get help with the software itself

There is no working upstream. Debian's package is the only support route, which is why the tracker is cited above rather than a project page.
